tasks.short: See who is due a follow-up, plan it with the counselee, hold the follow-up interview and record whether needs were met.

steps.what: Counselor goes through files to see who is due a follow-up
Counselor checks the list of counselees due a follow-up and the booking message before it goes
Counselor sends the checked booking links to those counselees from the guidance system
Counselee picks a follow-up time through the booking link
Counselor e-mails or phones counselees who did not pick a time to plan the follow-up
Counselor conducts follow-up interviews with counselees to determine if their needs have been met
Counselor writes the outcome of the follow-up in the file

tasks.design: The student guidance system ({OTHER}) sets a follow-up date when a counselling round closes and lists who is due; counselees get a link to pick a time. The counselor checks the list and sends the booking links. The outcome is written in the file as today; it is a first record and keeps its time. The interview itself stays as it is.
tasks.previous_blocker: Follow-ups depended on the counselor remembering and phoning.
tasks.enabler_now: Guidance systems hold follow-up dates, and booking links are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Counselees who struggle most often do not respond to links.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing in a short chat that a student's plan has quietly fallen apart.

ambition.what: Every counselee gets a three-question check-in message; those whose needs are not met are invited for an interview.

reach.task: Check on students after a change of course
reach.learn: Whether follow-up dates find dropouts earlier.

evidence.claim: Guidance and case systems can set follow-up dates and list who is due.
Notes about counselees can include special-category data and need strict access.

assumptions: Boundary: from listing follow-ups to the recorded outcome; new counselling rounds are outside.
Input contract: follow-up dates set by the counselor when closing a round; outcome fields agreed by the guidance team; fallback is memory and phone.
Interviews, the outcome record and the check and send of booking links keep their full time. About 60% of counselees book through the link; s2 keeps 40 for phoning the rest.
Counselees' time to pick a slot is shown in s2b and is outside the counselor's savings.
research_questions: Do more counselees get a follow-up with system dates?

incremental.description: Counselor sets the follow-up date when closing a round.

approvals.approved_version: The booking message and the list of counselees due a follow-up exactly as checked by the counselor in s1b, sent once from the guidance system to those counselees; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only a third of counselees book through the link, so s2 keeps 70 (13.7); high: about 60% book as assumed (17.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Run workshops and coaching on job search and interviews, comment on CVs and letters, hold mock interviews and share example materials.

steps.what: Counselor instructs individuals in job search and application strategies in workshops and coaching
Counselor reads each resume and letter and writes comments by hand

loop.input: The student's CV or letter, the vacancy text if any, and the guidance team's CV checklist.
loop.output: First-pass comments, each tied to a checklist item and a quoted line of the CV.
loop.check: Code drops any comment that does not name a checklist item or quote a line that exists in the CV; no comment may add or change facts about the student. The counselor reads each comment against its quoted line, drops those that do not fit, and edits and adds their own before the student sees anything.
loop.stop: One pass per document; the counselor finishes by hand if the pass fails.
loop.why_not_simpler: CVs are free text; a checklist alone cannot point to the lines that need work.

steps.what: Counselor checks the final comments on the CV or letter: each fits the quoted line and the student's goal
Counselor shares the checked comments with the student
Counselor runs mock interviews to build interview skills
Student opens example CVs, letters and vacancy links in the shared library
Counselor points students to the shared library and e-mails the few example materials it lacks: one by one for every student today

tasks.design: A bounded step gives first-pass comments on a CV or letter against the team's checklist, each tied to a quoted line, and the counselor edits and adds their own before the student sees them. Example materials sit in a shared library in {DOCS} that students can open; workshops, coaching and mock interviews stay in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every CV was read line by line from scratch, and examples were mailed one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models can comment on documents against a checklist; shared libraries are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Comments must fit the student and the job; students should learn, not copy.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a nervous student believe they are worth hiring.
tasks.altitude: The counselor edits first-pass comments instead of writing all of them.

reach.learn: Whether checklist comments raise CV quality before the counselor sees them.

evidence.claim: Language models can comment on a document against a checklist and quote the lines concerned.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes in education is high-risk; feedback that the counselor reviews and that grades nothing is outside that use.
Staff using AI tools must have sufficient AI literacy, a duty that applies now.

assumptions: Boundary: from coaching to materials shared; the student's applications are outside.
Input contract: CV checklist kept by the guidance team; CVs uploaded by students; example library kept by the counselor; fallback is reading by hand.

Workshops, mock interviews and the final check and sharing of comments do not change. s2 keeps 70 because the counselor still reads each CV and writes the advice that fits the student; first-pass comments cover the checklist points. Students opening the library (s4b) is about the effort of reading a mail.
No student data are used to train the model.
research_questions: How many first-pass comments do counselors keep?

incremental.description: Counselor keeps the CV checklist and example library current.

approvals.approved_version: The comments on that student's CV or letter exactly as checked by the counselor in s2b, shared once with that student; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most first-pass comments are rewritten, so s2 keeps 85, and students keep asking by mail, so s4 keeps 80 (4.3); high: comments and library as designed (10.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Talk about the student's needs, decide what help fits, find schemes and services, write the referral and check it was taken up.

steps.what: Counselor talks with the student about problems and needs
Counselor assesses needs for assistance such as financial aid, rehabilitation or extra vocational training
Counselor searches websites for training schemes, student finance rules and support services
Counselor writes the referral to the appropriate services in the form prefilled from the file
Counselor checks the final referral: what is asked, the student details shared, the recorded consent and the receiving service
Counselor sends the checked referral to the service
Counselor phones later to check whether the referral was taken up

tasks.design: A guide of schemes and services, kept by the guidance team in {DOCS} with conditions and contact persons, replaces searching websites. Referrals use a form in the student guidance system ({OTHER}) prefilled from the file with the student's recorded consent, and a reminder prompts the uptake check; talking and deciding stay with the counselor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service information was scattered and referrals written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared guides and prefilled forms are standard; guidance systems hold consent records.
tasks.still_hard: The guide must be kept current; schemes change each year.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a 'study problem' is really a problem at home.

reach.learn: Whether a shared guide reduces wrong referrals.

evidence.claim: Shared service guides and prefilled referral forms cut search and writing time.
Health and support needs are special-category data; referrals need the student's consent.
No decision with significant effect may be based solely on automated processing; the counselor decides.

assumptions: Boundary: from the needs talk to uptake checked; the services are outside.
Input contract: scheme and service guide kept by the guidance team's coordinator; consent recorded by the counselor; fallback is web search.
Coordinator time is outside the counselor's savings.

Talking, deciding, checking and sending the referral do not change. s4 keeps 70 because the counselor still writes why the student is referred; the form fills details from the file. s5 keeps 85 because the call stays; the reminder removes keeping a call list.
research_questions: Do more students take up referrals with a check?

incremental.description: Guidance coordinator keeps the guide current.

approvals.approved_version: The referral with its request and the student details shared exactly as checked by the counselor in s4b, with the student's recorded consent, sent once to the named service; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the guide covers only about half of the needs, so s3 keeps 75 (8.8); high: the guide as designed (12.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the year's career events, recruit employers and alumni, make invitations, handle sign-ups and reminders, and host the events.

steps.what: Counselor plans career workshops, job fairs and work experience programs with colleagues
Counselor looks up and contacts employers and alumni to take part
Counselor makes invitations and posters to promote each event
Counselor checks the final invitation, poster and sign-up confirmation text: event, date, place, speakers and the sign-up link
Counselor publishes the checked invitations and posters to students
Student signs up for the event in the registration form
Counselor handles sign-ups for each event: checks the list and answers questions
Counselor checks the reminder before it goes: event, date, place and the attendee list
Counselor releases the checked reminder from the registration form to all who signed up
Counselor hosts the career events

tasks.design: Employer and alumni contacts with their past participation sit in a small {CRM}, so recruiting starts from who said yes before. Invitations and posters come from event templates, and a registration form takes sign-ups and sends confirmations; the counselor checks and publishes the promotion and checks and releases each reminder; planning and hosting stay with the counselor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contacts were in personal mailboxes, and each event's promotion and sign-ups were done by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Small CRMs, templates and registration forms with reminders are standard tools.
tasks.still_hard: Employers' willingness depends on relationships; templates can make events look the same.
tasks.human_edge: Matching a shy student with the one employer who will inspire them.

reach.learn: Whether a shared employer list fills placements faster.

evidence.claim: Registration forms with automatic confirmations and reminders are standard tools.
Employer and student contact details are personal data; keep them only with a clear purpose.

assumptions: Boundary: from planning to hosting; event budgets are outside.
Input contract: employer and alumni contacts entered by the counselors with consent; templates kept by the counselor; fallback is mailboxes and manual sign-ups.

Planning, hosting and the checks before promotion and reminders go out do not change. s3 keeps 70 because the counselor still writes each event's text; templates give layout and standard parts. Students' sign-up time is shown in s4b.
Employers' time is outside the counselor's savings.

incremental.description: Counselor records employer participation after each event.

approvals.approved_version: The reminder with event, date and place and the attendee list exactly as checked by the counselor in s6a, sent once from the registration form to those signed up; any change needs a new check.
The invitation, poster and confirmation text with event, date, place, speakers and sign-up link exactly as checked by the counselor in s3b, published once to students; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few contacts in the CRM yet and posters mostly made by hand, so s2 keeps 85 and s3 keeps 85 (15.2); high: CRM and templates as designed (21.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The career counselor keeps coaching, judgement and events; follow-up planning, CV first passes, searching and sign-ups shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A counselor who follows up with every student and spends saved time on the ones who need it most.

job.title: Educational, Guidance, and Career Counselors and Advisors
